findings.element: How we get the data after choosing a non-clearing Stripe account (Stripe fees / Business Checking)
findings.finding: Choosing a non-clearing account silently switches both sides to a one-option 'Manual' with two required uploads, and nothing on the page says why; the integration upload's only guidance is 'How to get this file', which names no file.
findings.user_impact: A user who expected Stripe to pull its data suddenly faces a QuickBooks GL export and an unnamed Stripe file with no explanation, so they can't tell whether they picked the wrong account or which Stripe export to fetch, and at a create step with a 73.6% drop that is a likely point of abandonment.
findings.suggested_fix: When the account forces manual mode, show an inline note in the data section such as 'This account isn't the Stripe clearing account, so both files must be uploaded; pick Stripe mzkt.by for automatic retrieval', and name the exact Stripe export in the how-to label.

evidence.action: Select Integration = mzkt.by (Stripe), then Account = Stripe fees (and again with Business Checking)
evidence.observed: Data section shows 'Accounting … Import method * Manual … Upload file * How to get General ledger export from QuickBooks Online' and 'Integration … Import method * Manual … Upload file * How to get this file'; toggle hidden=true; no explanatory text anywhere in the visible card text

findings.element: Accounting-side Import method under the 'Synder accounts (manual file upload required)' group
findings.finding: The same account group gives opposite results for the QuickBooks side: a manual-group Stripe account forces QuickBooks to Manual with a GL upload, while every manual-group PayPal or Shopify account leaves QuickBooks on 'Automated (recommended)' with no upload.
findings.user_impact: Users can't predict what a 'manual file upload required' account will ask of them, and after switching integrations the QuickBooks requirement appears or disappears with no explanation, which undermines trust in the group label that is meant to explain the consequence.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the QuickBooks-side rule the same for all manual-group accounts, or split the group labels so they say exactly which side needs a file (for example 'integration file upload required').

evidence.action: Select Stripe + Stripe fees; then select PayPal + PayPal clearing; then Shopify + Shopify clearing (Synder)
evidence.observed: Stripe fees: Accounting 'Import method * Manual', GL export upload required. PayPal and Shopify: every account sits under 'Synder accounts (manual file upload required)', yet Accounting shows 'Import method * Automated (recommended) / Manual' with no upload zone

findings.element: Period > Custom start/end date inputs, and the Run reconciliation status
findings.finding: Custom ranges entirely in the future (Nov 1–30) and ranges ending today (Sep 1–25) are accepted and the run starts, and the 'Reconciliation started' status never shows which period, integration or account was submitted.
findings.user_impact: A user who mistypes a month launches a reconciliation with no data, or one that breaks the no-today rule, and the confirmation gives them no chance to notice before waiting hours for a useless result.
findings.suggested_fix: Cap the date inputs at yesterday and refuse ranges that reach today or the future with an inline error, and have the started status repeat the submitted period, account and integration.

evidence.action: Stripe + clearing chosen, Date range = Custom, enter Nov 1–30 then Run; repeat with Sep 1–25
evidence.observed: future-only: error "", started=true, hint '2026-11-01 – 2026-11-30'; ending today: error "", started=true; input min="" max=""; status text only 'Reconciliation started / Synder is gathering and processing your transactions.'

findings.element: 'Set import methods' toggle link on the automatic retrieval card
findings.finding: Clicking 'Set import methods', which reads like 'review or adjust', silently changes the Stripe side from the recommended Automated to Assisted and adds two required uploads.
findings.user_impact: A user who only wanted to see the methods now can't run: Run blocks with 'Upload the required file' until they notice and switch back to Automated or click 'Use automatic retrieval'.
findings.suggested_fix: Open the manual panel with the current effective methods kept (Stripe = Automated) so that nothing new becomes required until the user changes a method.

evidence.action: Stripe + Stripe mzkt.by (clearing) on the automatic card, click 'Set import methods'
evidence.observed: Integration Import method value after toggle: Assisted; panel now shows 'Upload file * How to get Balance change from the activity from Stripe' and 'Upload file * How to get Payouts from Stripe'; Run with a file missing gives the error 'Upload the required file'

findings.element: Run error banner when an upload is missing
findings.finding: When one of two required uploads is missing, the banner says only 'Upload the required file' and names neither the file nor the side, unlike the empty-form error, which names its field.
findings.user_impact: With two drop zones per side, the user has to scan every upload zone to find the missing one, which recreates the vague error that round 1 fixed for fields.
findings.suggested_fix: Name the missing file and side in the banner (for example 'Upload the Stripe Payouts report') and mark that drop zone as invalid.

evidence.action: Stripe + clearing, Set import methods (Assisted), Browse one of the two Stripe files, click Run reconciliation
evidence.observed: error 'Upload the required file'; no file or side named; the empty-form Run by contrast shows 'Select an integration' and marks Integration invalid

gaps: Changing the integration or account after files are uploaded was never exercised: the map records the account being cleared and the data section hidden on an integration switch, but not whether uploads are discarded without the confirm that 'Use automatic retrieval' shows, or whether any notice explains the cleared account.
Switching from a non-clearing account back to a clearing account with uploaded files: whether files are lost silently is unknown.
Run on PayPal or Shopify (Assisted/Manual) was never exercised end to end, so their blocked and started states are unverified.

Retrieval failures and sync-precondition errors (KF-9: missing mappings, multi-currency off, closed period, lost QBO auth) are not implemented, so whether the design names the failed precondition and the fix cannot be judged.
Overlapping-period rejection for the same clearing account (domain rule) was never exercised.
